rows.citation: Daly AC, Gavaghan DJ, Holmes C, et al. (2015). Hodgkin-Huxley revisited: reparametrization and identifiability analysis of the classic action potential model with approximate Bayesian methods. Royal Society Open Science.
rows.model_type: Hodgkin-Huxley conductance-based single-compartment action potential model (CellML, run via Chaste functional curation), framed for cardiac cell modelling
rows.controlled_mutations: no - parameter sets are sampled from ABC posteriors; no deliberate single-fault edits, although posterior variants act like parameter perturbations.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - fitted to voltage-clamp data, then posterior models run under four more complex Hodgkin-Huxley voltage protocols and a current-clamp test.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - RMSE distance between simulated and reference traces; no eFEL-style spike features.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - protocols come from the original 1952 experiments; the paper only suggests richer protocols could constrain parameters.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - posterior models examined on protocols not used for fitting; no held-out models or fault families.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-assisted model edits studied.
rows.software: Chaste HodgkinHuxleyABC paper tutorial, https://chaste.github.io/docs/paper-tutorials/ (the paper's chaste.cs.ox.ac.uk trac URL now redirects there)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Parameter inference and identifiability, not change detection. NeuroSem would add single-fault mutants, current-clamp feature batteries, refinement-calibrated tolerances, protocol selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (10.1098/rsos.150499); Europe PMC REST (PMID 27019736) and PMC4807457 full-text XML (methods, code availability); Chaste paper-tutorials page fetched
rows.found_via: PubMed E-utilities 'ICGenealogy OR ion channel genealogy' | WebSearch Groenendaal query; WebSearch Semantic Scholar-style query; Crossref

rows.citation: Daunizeau J, Preuschoff K, Friston K, et al. (2011). Optimizing Experimental Design for Comparing Models of Brain Function. PLoS Computational Biology.
rows.model_type: Dynamic causal models (DCM) of fMRI network dynamics; macroscale Bayesian model comparison
rows.controlled_mutations: no - compares predefined candidate network models, not seeded faults or edited models.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - evaluates alternative experimental designs (e.g., epoch duration, stimulation site) for each model-comparison question.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - fMRI time series; no single-cell electrophysiology features.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - chooses designs that minimise model-selection error using a derived Laplace-Chernoff risk.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - Monte-Carlo simulations plus empirical fMRI from a bimanual motor task check predictions; no held-out model or fault families.
rows.software: SPM (paper states the routines will be implemented there), http://www.fil.ion.ucl.ac.uk/spm/
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Principled design optimisation for discriminating hypotheses. NeuroSem instead selects current-clamp protocols empirically by mutant coverage for regression detection in NeuroML neurons, tested on held-out models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (10.1371/journal.pcbi.1002280); Europe PMC REST (PMID 22125485) abstract and PMC3219623 full-text XML (methods, software note)
rows.found_via: PubMed E-utilities 'optimal experimental design[tiab] AND neuron'

rows.citation: Ogino M, Sekizawa D, Kitazono J, et al. (2025). Designing optimal perturbation inputs for system identification in neuroscience. bioRxiv (preprint).
rows.model_type: Linear dynamical (first-order VAR-type) network models of macroscale neural activity; connectivity-matrix estimation
rows.controlled_mutations: no - no faults or model edits; the target is estimating a connectivity matrix.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - relates designed perturbations to impulse, step and sinusoidal inputs (TMS, tDCS, tACS analogues) and compares against passive observation.
rows.electrophysiology_features: no - uses state time series and estimation error, not voltage or spike features.
rows.protocol_optimization: yes - derives inputs that minimise asymptotic connectivity-estimation error through the state covariance.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - simulated state classification uses 10-fold cross-validation; no held-out models or fault families.
rows.software: none located (no code or repository link found in the v5 full-text XML)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Conceptual support that perturbations reveal hidden dynamics. NeuroSem targets edit detection in nonlinear single-neuron NeuroML models using current-clamp batteries, mutants and calibrated tolerances, not system identification.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (posted-content); bioRxiv details API (5 versions, 2025-03-07 to 2026-06-12, CC BY-NC); Europe PMC PPR986244 abstract; v5 JATS XML scanned. Input v2 URL returned HTTP 429, so DOI URL used.
rows.found_via: WebSearch site:biorxiv.org (optimal current clamp stimulus protocol design ...; perturbation fingerprint ...)

rows.citation: Valadez-Godínez S, Sossa H, Santiago-Montero R (2020). On the accuracy and computational cost of spiking neuron implementation. Neural Networks.
rows.model_type: Spiking point-neuron models: Hodgkin-Huxley (direct and tabulated rate functions), Izhikevich, leaky integrate-and-fire
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - systematically varies simulation parameters and table discretisation, but these are benchmark settings, not single-fault mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - constant and random input currents under balanced, lower and upper boundary conditions in regular-spiking mode.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - normalised accuracy metrics; argues firing frequency alone is insufficient to judge simulation accuracy.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - multiobjective optimisation targets simulation parameters (accuracy versus cost), not stimulus protocols.
rows.heldout_evaluation: unclear - abstract only; no held-out split described there, full text not accessed.
rows.software: unclear - not stated in the abstract; full text (Elsevier) not accessed
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Relevant background for numerical mutants and refinement tolerances. NeuroSem treats numerical changes as one fault family inside a detection and protocol-selection framework, not as accuracy-cost benchmarking.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (vol 122, pp 196-217); Europe PMC REST (PMID 31689679) abstract; doi.org resolves to Elsevier linkinghub (full text not read)
rows.found_via: PubMed E-utilities 'time step[tiab] AND neuron model AND numerical accuracy'

rows.citation: Chen TY, Ho JWK, Liu H, et al. (2009). An innovative approach for testing bioinformatics programs using metamorphic testing. BMC Bioinformatics.
rows.model_type: General bioinformatics software: gene network simulator (GNLab) and short-read mapper (SeqMap)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - random single-statement mutants (AOR, CR, ROR, SVR); equivalent mutants excluded, leaving nine GNLab and three SeqMap non-equivalent mutants.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - several metamorphic relations and test-case batches (random, yeast, E. coli inputs); not physiological stimuli.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - tabulates which relations detect which mutants but does not select a compact subset.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - all mutants and relations analysed together.
rows.software: none (no testing tool released; subject programs GNLab and SeqMap 1.0.8, URLs not verified)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Shares mutant-based evaluation and a relation-by-mutant detection table. NeuroSem adds neuron stimuli, eFEL features, refinement-calibrated tolerances, greedy battery selection, random baselines and held-out models and fault families.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (vol 10, article 24); Europe PMC REST (PMID 19152705) abstract and PMC2657898 full-text XML (mutation analysis section)
rows.found_via: PubMed E-utilities 'metamorphic testing[tiab]' | OpenAlex search 'metamorphic testing bioinformatics'; cited in WebSearch site:dl.acm.org metamorphic testing bioinformatics snippet | WebSearch metamorphic testing SBML query; Crossref title query

rows.citation: Peng Z, Lin X, Simon M, et al. (2021). Unit and regression tests of scientific software: A study on SWMM. Journal of Computational Science.
rows.model_type: General scientific simulation software (EPA Storm Water Management Model, SWMM)
rows.controlled_mutations: yes - 150 single-fault mutants (arithmetic and relational operator replacement) on statements changed between SWMM 5.1.013 and 5.1.014.
rows.multiple_stimuli: partial - 58 regression input (.inp) files grouped by folder; hydrological inputs, not neural stimuli.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - prioritises regression-test groups by coverage Jaccard distance and tracks cumulative mutation score; no budgeted subset selection or random baselines.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - prioritisation assessed on the same version change; no held-out systems or fault families.
rows.software: none (no study tool located; paper says SWMM's own tests are on GitHub, URL not verified)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest in spirit: mutation-scored regression-test prioritisation in scientific software. NeuroSem targets NeuroML neurons with stimulus protocols, feature tolerances, cost-matched random baselines and held-out models.
rows.verification_method: Crossref API (vol 53, article 101347); Europe PMC REST (PMID 34017363) abstract; PMC8128694 author-manuscript HTML full text (regression-test and mutation sections); doi.org resolves to Elsevier
